primary_text_note: Full text downloaded to scripts/_retrofc/_texts/animal-farm.txt from Project Gutenberg Australia (ebook 0100011). Every quotation in the unit was grepped against it.

findings.claim: 'In the AQA exam, you will answer on Animal Farm in Section B of Paper 2 (Modern Texts). You will be given an extract and asked to write about the extract and the whole novel.'
findings.truth: Modern texts is the FIRST section of that paper, not the second, and no extract is printed. It is one closed-book essay chosen from two questions, 30 marks plus 4 for SPaG.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md, 'Specification at a glance' - Paper 2: Modern texts and poetry, 2h15, 96 marks; 'Section A Modern texts: students will answer one essay question from a choice of two on their studied modern prose or drama text'; no extract is printed and the assessments are closed book. Modern text essay = 30 marks + 4 SPaG, AO1 12 / AO2 12 / AO3 6.

findings.claim: Eleven practice questions are labelled '30+4 marks - Shakespeare Essay' (L1 items 0 and 4, and item 2 in every other lesson).
findings.truth: Animal Farm is a modern prose set text, not a Shakespeare play. Relabelled '30+4 marks - Modern Text Essay', which is the label the other 49 questions in this unit already use.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md, 'Specification at a glance' - Paper 2: Modern texts and poetry, 2h15, 96 marks; 'Section A Modern texts: students will answer one essay question from a choice of two on their studied modern prose or drama text'; no extract is printed and the assessments are closed book. Modern text essay = 30 marks + 4 SPaG, AO1 12 / AO2 12 / AO3 6. Precedent: the same relabel was applied in english-literature-aqa__a-taste-of-honey.

findings.truth: No extract is printed for the modern text. Each stem rewritten as a whole-text essay question; the L1 mark scheme now says 'the early idealism'.

findings.claim: Rule of three: 'No animal in England knows the meaning of happiness or leisure or retirement'.
findings.truth: Fabricated. Old Major says 'No animal in England knows the meaning of happiness or leisure after he is a year old.' There is no 'or retirement', and the line is not a tricolon. Replaced with a real tricolon from the same speech: 'our lives are miserable, laborious, and short'.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 1, lines 121-122 and 116-117.

findings.claim: 'Is it not crystal clear, comrades?' (content and flashcard 4).
findings.truth: The line reads 'Is it not crystal clear, then, comrades, that all the evils of this life of ours spring from the tyranny of human beings?' The word 'then' was dropped.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 1, line 170.

findings.claim: Squealer: 'It has been proved by science, comrades, that a pig's metabolism requires apples and milk.'
findings.truth: Fabricated - the word 'metabolism' never appears in the novella. Squealer's real line is 'Milk and apples (this has been proved by Science, comrades) contain substances absolutely necessary to the well-being of a pig.'
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 3, lines 726-728.

findings.claim: 'Surely, comrades, you do not want Jones to come back?' (content and flashcard 6).
findings.truth: The line reads 'Surely, comrades, you do not want Jones back?' The words 'to come' are not in it.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 5, lines 1149-1150.

findings.claim: Snowball's plan is 'a feigned retreat to lure the men into the yard, followed by an ambush from three sides' (content and flashcard 7).
findings.truth: The ambush party - three horses, three cows and the rest of the pigs - had been lying in the cowshed and emerged in the men's rear, cutting them off. That is why the battle is named after the cowshed. 'Three sides' is invented.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 4, lines 840-843 and 906-908.

findings.claim: 'Orwell shows that Napoleon never gives a single public speech after seizing power. All communication goes through Squealer.' (Key Fact and flashcard 5.)
findings.truth: False. Napoleon speaks in public repeatedly after the coup - he announces the end of the Sunday Meetings, pronounces the death sentence on Snowball, and 'ended his speech with his usual cry of Long live Animal Farm!'. Orwell's actual point is that he 'was not seen in public as often as once in a fortnight' and that 'All orders were now issued through Squealer'.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 5 line 1311; ch. 6 line 1441; ch. 8 lines 1850-1852; ch. 9 line 2542; ch. 10 line 2819.

findings.claim: The pigs 'supervised and directed' from a distance (content and flashcard 5).
findings.truth: The novella reads 'The pigs did not actually work, but directed and supervised the others.' The two words are the wrong way round inside quotation marks.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 3, line 557.

findings.claim: 'Orwell describes her looking out over the landscape that "ought to have been a scene of tranquillity."'
findings.truth: Fabricated - the phrase appears nowhere in the novella. Orwell writes 'It was a clear spring evening' and 'Never had the farm... appeared to the animals so desirable a place.' The animals also go to the knoll by the half-built windmill together; Clover does not climb a hill alone.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 7, lines 1723-1725 and 1699-1703.

findings.claim: Key Fact: Clover 'would have protested if she could have found the right words', with a revision prompt asking for 'Clover's exact words about protesting'. Knowledge check 4 and flashcard 14 repeat it.
findings.truth: Misattributed. 'Some of them would have protested if they could have found the right arguments' describes the other animals in chapter 5. Clover's line here is 'Such were her thoughts, though she lacked the words to express them', and Orwell states 'There was no thought of rebellion or disobedience in her mind.'
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 5 line 1118; ch. 7 lines 1764-1765 and 1772-1773.

findings.claim: After 'Beasts of England' is banned, 'A new anthem praising Napoleon replaces it' (content and flashcard 13).
findings.truth: The replacement praises the FARM: Minimus's song 'Animal Farm, Animal Farm, / Never through me shalt thou come to harm!' Minimus's poem in praise of Napoleon is a separate, later piece, written in chapter 8.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 7, lines 1805-1810; ch. 8, lines 1875-1877.

findings.claim: 'His portrait replaces the commandments.' Flashcard 4 asks 'What poem replaces the Seven Commandments on the barn wall?' and the mark scheme for practice question 1 rewards 'the replacement of commandments with Napoleon's image'.
findings.truth: Nothing replaces the Seven Commandments until chapter 10. Minimus's poem is 'inscribed on the wall of the big barn, at the opposite end from the Seven Commandments', surmounted by a portrait of Napoleon. The lesson's own earlier paragraph says exactly this, so the lesson contradicted itself.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 8, lines 1875-1880; ch. 10, lines 2725-2727.

findings.claim: Napoleon 'always enters from a different door to the other pigs' (content and flashcard 5).
findings.truth: Invented - no door detail exists. Orwell says Napoleon 'inhabited separate apartments from the others. He took his meals alone, with two dogs to wait upon him, and always ate from the Crown Derby dinner service.'
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 8, lines 1855-1858.

findings.claim: 'He is now twelve years old - past the retirement age he was promised under Animalism.'
findings.truth: Boxer is not yet twelve. 'Boxer's twelfth birthday was due in the late summer of the following year', and twelve is the retiring age fixed for horses. He collapses just SHORT of the pension he was promised, which is the point of the irony.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 9, lines 2239-2249.

findings.claim: Boxer 'looks forward to spending his remaining years in the pasture that Old Major had promised all retiring animals would enjoy' (content and flashcard 2).
findings.truth: Old Major never promises a retirement pasture. The home of rest for animals past work was voted at a Sunday Meeting after the Rebellion, and the grazing-ground was still only a rumour in chapter 9.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 3, lines 631-634; ch. 9, lines 2243-2246.

findings.claim: Clover cries out: 'Boxer! Boxer! Boxer! Get out! Get out quickly! They're taking you to your death!'
findings.truth: Not a continuous quotation. Clover first cries 'Boxer! Boxer! Boxer!' as she chases the van; the second, separate cry is 'Boxer! Get out! Get out quickly! They're taking you to your death!' Trimmed to the real continuous line, and the flashcard now carries it in full.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 9, lines 2474-2481.

findings.claim: 'Benjamin is the only animal besides the pigs who can read fluently' (content and knowledge check 3).
findings.truth: Muriel 'could read somewhat better than the dogs' and reads the commandments aloud; the dogs 'learned to read fairly well'. Orwell's wording is that Benjamin 'could read as well as any pig, but never exercised his faculty'.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 3, lines 480-500 (the reading classes); ch. 3, Benjamin's literacy.

findings.claim: 'One morning, Clover neighs in alarm...' before the pigs walk on two legs.
findings.truth: It happens in the evening: 'on a pleasant evening when the animals had finished work and were making their way back to the farm buildings, that the terrified neighing of a horse sounded from the yard.'
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 10, lines 2673-2678.

findings.claim: The confessors after the four pigs are given as 'hens, geese, a sheep'.
findings.truth: Three hens, ONE goose, then one sheep and two more sheep. 'Geese' plural is wrong and there is more than one sheep. Not mark-affecting, so left alone.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 7, lines 1701-1710.

findings.claim: 'Orwell reveals that Napoleon used the money from selling Boxer to the knacker to buy a case of whisky.'
findings.truth: Orwell keeps this as rumour, not revelation: 'the word went round that from somewhere or other the pigs had acquired the money to buy themselves another case of whisky.' It is the standard and intended reading, so no edit, but 'reveals' overstates the text.
findings.evidence: Project Gutenberg Australia, Animal Farm (ebook 0100011), full text; ch. 9, lines 2548-2553.

findings.claim: 'Russia defeated Germany but suffered 27 million casualties.'
findings.truth: The 27 million figure is Soviet DEATHS, not casualties (casualties include the wounded and would be far higher). Left as is because the sense is clear, but 'deaths' would be the accurate word.
findings.evidence: Standard Russian Academy of Sciences figure, ~26.6 million Soviet war dead.

summary: All ten lessons carry findings. The unit was built against the wrong question format: eleven practice questions are labelled 'Shakespeare Essay', four more tell the student to 'read the extract', and three exam tips promise a printed extract - the AQA modern text question is one closed-book essay chosen from two, 30 marks plus 4 for SPaG, with no extract. Five quotations are fabricated or misattributed (Old Major's 'or retirement', Squealer's 'metabolism', Clover's 'scene of tranquillity' and her 'right words', Napoleon's 'different door'), and three plot claims are wrong (Napoleon never speaks in public; the poem replaces the commandments; Boxer is already twelve). All 52 edits are surgical and every replacement quotation was verified line by line against the full text.
